scope: Writing-stage inventory, not a completed paper or a global impossibility theorem.

classification_definitions.primitive_value_obstruction: An archived proof bounds the actual primitive integer value or reduced denominator in the specified family; reading status is separate.
classification_definitions.arithmetic_theorem: A local valuation, denominator or content statement; not necessarily a global primitive-value obstruction.
classification_definitions.analytic_theorem: A real-size theorem; arithmetic may still be missing.
classification_definitions.structural_obstruction: A proved limitation of a particular construction or implication.
classification_definitions.structural_theorem: An exact structural description, not necessarily an obstruction.
classification_definitions.estimate_limitation: The stated bound or normalization fails; actual primitive values may remain unsettled.
classification_definitions.finite_evidence: Exact or interval calculations at finitely many prescribed instances.
classification_definitions.positive_construction: An identity or positive/nonzero family; this alone does not prove irrationality.
classification_definitions.partial_construction: Some proof ingredients are available, with an explicit missing ingredient.
classification_definitions.attributed_identity: Prior published or externally attributed input.
classification_definitions.equivalence: An exact reduction to a known or previously archived construction.
classification_definitions.standard_fact: General established algebra, not an originality claim.

claims.title: A positive cubic-tail kernel isolating beta(4)
claims.statement: Write theta=beta(4) and S_l(a)=sum_{j=0}^{a-1}((4j+1)^(-l)-(4j+3)^(-l)). For positive integer a,b, K(a^2,b^2)=[b S_3(b)-a S_3(a)]/[6(b^2-a^2)] off the diagonal and K(a^2,a^2)=theta-S_4(a)+S_3(a)/(12a). It has the Stieltjes product representation with density omega(s)=pi^2 s^2(1+A-2A^3)/96, A=sech(2pi s), and every ordered square minor is strictly positive. K(0,0)=2theta gives a continuous zero-node extension.
claims.limitations: This is an explicitly defined kernel. It does not classify all positive representations of beta(4). The general positivity mechanism is classical.

claims.title: Uniform two-sided comparison with a Cauchy determinant
claims.statement: For increasing positive integer row nodes a_i and column nodes b_j, let C_ij=1/(a_i+b_j), c0=pi^3/192, M=1+2/(3sqrt(6)), tau=1/(sqrt(2)pi). Then [c0/(1+tau)^2]^n det C <= det K <= (M c0)^n det C. Thus log det K=log det C+O(n) uniformly in the node locations. The proof evaluates the regularized Cauchy determinant exactly by a rank-one update.
claims.limitations: The constants and uniform comparison concern C01; an entrywise comparison alone would not establish this statement. The common-zero case has a separate formula in the proof.

claims.title: Primitive growth for every consecutive principal offset
claims.statement: Let Q_{n,m}(X)=det(XI+R) be C01 on a_i=m+i, 1<=i<=n, with theta replaced by X, and let Z_{n,m}=H_{n,m}Q_{n,m} be primitive in Z[X] with H>0. For every sequence of integers m_n>=0, liminf n^(-2)log Z_{n,m_n}(theta)>=2-2log 2>0. For any principal positive node set with maximum M0 and prime 2M0<p<4M0, p>=5, the coefficient of X^(n-r_p), r_p=#{i:4a_i>p}, has valuation -4r_p. This is a valuation of an actual coefficient. The nodes 0,...,n-1 have the same limiting lower bound.
claims.limitations: Excludes these full principal pencils, including rational invertible changes of their bases. Does not exclude sparse nodes, nonprincipal minors, different subspaces, weights or combinations of determinants.

claims.title: Difference-variable Gram moments with full target rank
claims.statement: Let J(P)=integral_[0,1]^2 P(u,v)log^2(uv)/(sqrt(uv)(1+uv))du dv and mu_m=J((u-v)^(2m))/96. With C_m=binom(2m,m), T_s(j)=sum_{k<j}(-1)^k/(2k+1)^s, mu_m=C_m theta+B_m, where B_m=-C_m T_4(m)+(1/6)sum_{j=0,j!=m}^{2m}binom(2m,j)T_3(j)/(j-m). The Hankel polynomial Q_n(X)=det[C_{i+j}X+B_{i+j}]_{i,j<n} has degree n, leading coefficient 2^(n-1), and Q_n(theta)>0.
claims.limitations: Formal coefficient identity; it assumes no independence or irrationality of theta. The full-rank coefficient is specific to the difference-variable construction.

claims.title: Exact large-prime primitive exponent for the difference Gram
claims.statement: Let Z_n=kappa_n Q_n be primitive in Z[X], kappa_n>0 rational. For every prime p>4n, v_p(kappa_n)=3 max(0,2n-2-floor(p/4)). The leading residue block is anti-triangular with nonzero anti-diagonal; its complementary theta coefficient is a p-unit. The only possible negative valuation of kappa_n is at 2 and is at least -(n-1).
claims.limitations: The exact formula covers p>4n; it is not a formula for every prime. It already includes the full coefficient content, rather than just a sufficient denominator.

claims.title: Primitive invariance under full rational basis changes
claims.statement: Multiplying a full rational matrix pencil on either side by an invertible rational matrix multiplies its determinant by a nonzero rational scalar. Its primitive integer polynomial is therefore unchanged up to sign. Multiplying a rational linear form by a common nonzero rational scalar likewise leaves its primitive pair unchanged.
claims.limitations: Selecting a proper subspace, changing the measure or changing the pencil is not such a basis change.
claims.novelty_assessment: Standard framework or elementary consequence; do not present as an original general theorem.

claims.title: The complete cone of scalar positive polynomial forms
claims.statement: For I(P)=(1/6)integral_0^1 (-log x)^3 P(x^2)/(1+x^2)dx, rational P nonnegative on [0,1] yields A=P(-1), B=nu((P-P(-1))/(1+t)), dnu=(-log t)^3dt/(96sqrt(t)). Its image is {0} union {(A,B) in Q^2:A theta+B>0}. At each fixed degree the image is the rational cone between two explicitly computed extremal rays; the least witness degree for a small positive form L is log(|A|/L)/log(3+2sqrt(2))+O(log log(|A|/L)).
claims.limitations: Representation of an already specified positive rational form is not a way to produce small integral forms. Classical interval sum-of-squares and Schur-complement ingredients require attribution.
